title: Retrospective analysis of DDAVP response in patients with von Willebrand Disease
summary:
Von Willebrand Disease (VWD) is the most common hereditary bleeding disorder. It is caused by a deficiency or dysfunction of the von Willebrand factor, an important component of primary hemostasis and also the carrier protein for  coagulation factor VIII. Depending on the VWD type and severity, the disease is associated with an increased tendency for mucosal bleeding, easy bruising, and prolonged bleeding after surgical procedures. 

To treat or prevent bleeding during surgery or after injuries, Desmopressin (DDAVP) is often used, as it can induce the release of the body’s own stored reserves of von Willebrand factor into the bloodstream. However, because the response to this treatment varies significantly between individuals the DDAVP test is routinely performed to evaluate its effectiveness for each patient. This test measures blood levels before and at 1, 2 and 3 hours post administration.

The aim of this study is to retrospectively analyse the results of the DDAVP tests to better understand why some patients respond better than others investigating the influence of factors like VW subtype, age, sex or hormonal status. This serves to improve the individualized therapy in events of surgery or injuries.

The study evaluates data from patients at the Hemophilia Center of Frankfurt University Hospital who underwent a DDAVP test between 01/2015 and 11/2025.
The analysis includes laboratory parameters such as VWF activity, VWF antigen and Factor VIII levels before and after medication. In addition, the patients’ bleeding symptoms are recorded, particularly in relation to bleeding complications during surgical procedures as well as their family history.
An additional focus is to determine whether the 1-hour measurement is sufficient or if additional time points improve diagnostic accuracy. 
Furthermore, we will specifically address the hormonal influence on desmopression response by comparing result in women before and after menopause.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients with von Willebrand Disease type 1, 2A or 2M and DDAVP-test in period 2015 to 2025

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients. with confirmed von Willebrand Disease type 1, 2A or 2 M (according to ISTH   
   criteria) 
• conduction of DDAVP test
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients without confirmed von Willebrand Disease and patients with von Willebrand Disease type 2B, 3 
• Patients with seizures, cardiovascular diseases, hypertension, or taking diuretics
• Patienten with maligne, lymphoproliferative and autoimmunologic
   diseases and patients undergoing valproate therapy
• Patients with current pregnancy
